title: Flywheel Review 2026: Pricing, Plans and Who It Suits
excerpt: Flywheel starts at $25 a month on annual billing, with free migrations, nightly backups and billing transfer for clients. Here is what each plan costs, how it tested and who it suits.

meta.rl_r_cta_head: Moving a live site to Flywheel?
meta.rl_r_cta_sub: Reinforce Lab can copy, test and switch your WordPress site without lost rankings.
meta._yoast_wpseo_title: Flywheel Review 2026: Pricing, Plans and Who It Suits
meta._yoast_wpseo_metadesc: Flywheel review for 2026: plans and prices, WordPress features for designers and agencies, who it suits and how to set up your first site step by step.
meta.rl_answer: Flywheel is managed WordPress hosting for designers and agencies, owned by WP Engine. Plans start at $25 a month on annual billing for one site, with nightly backups, free migrations and 24/7 chat support. It suits client work and costs more than shared hosting.
meta.rl_faqs:
What is Flywheel hosting? | Flywheel is managed WordPress hosting for designers and agencies, owned by WP Engine. It runs the servers, caching, backups and security, and adds tools for client work such as Blueprints and billing transfer.
How much does Flywheel cost? | On Flywheel's pricing page on 20 November 2026, Starter was $25 a month on annual billing ($30 monthly) for one site with 25,000 visits. Freelance was $96 ($115 monthly) for up to 10 sites. Agency was $242 ($290 monthly) for up to 30 sites.
Does Flywheel raise its price at renewal? | The pricing page shows one price per plan. A third-party review says Flywheel does not raise prices at renewal. Check your order summary to be sure.
Is Flywheel good for hosting? | Yes for freelancers and agencies. Independent tests saw load times near one second and uptime above 99.9%. It costs more than shared hosting for one small site.
Does Flywheel have a money-back guarantee? | Flywheel's home page lists a 60-day money-back guarantee. Read the terms at checkout.
Will Flywheel move my site for free? | Yes. Flywheel migrates your sites for free, and it says the copy is usually ready to review in 24 to 48 hours.
Can I host multiple WordPress sites on one Flywheel account? | Yes. Freelance covers up to 10 sites and Agency up to 30. Extra sites cost $20 a month or $200 a year.
Does Flywheel include email hosting or domain names? | No. Flywheel is WordPress hosting only. Buy a domain from a registrar and use a separate email service.
Does Flywheel have caching? | Yes. Every plan includes FlyCache, which Flywheel tunes for common plugins and themes, and a Fastly CDN.
Can I install premium plugins on Flywheel? | Yes, with some limits. Flywheel runs managed WordPress, so a short list of plugins that clash with its caching or security is blocked. Check its help docs for the current list.
Is Local by Flywheel the same as Flywheel hosting? | No. Local is a free tool that runs WordPress on your computer. It works with any host and connects to Flywheel to push a site live. Flywheel hosting is the paid plan.
What happens if my Flywheel site gets more visits than my plan allows? | Flywheel does not shut the site off. It charges $1 for each 1,000 extra visits and $1 for each extra GB of storage.
Who should avoid Flywheel? | Owners of one small blog who want the lowest price, people who need email hosting in the same plan, and anyone who wants a published uptime guarantee.

meta.rl_takeaways:
Starter is $25 a month on annual billing, $30 monthly, for one site with 25,000 visits (Flywheel, 20 Nov 2026).
Free migrations, nightly backups kept 30 days and 24/7 chat support come with every plan.
Independent tests saw load times near one second and uptime above 99.9%.
Flywheel has no email hosting and no domain names, and it charges $1 per 1,000 extra visits.
meta.rl_r_verdict: Flywheel is a good fit for freelancers and agencies that host client sites and want managed care, backups and billing transfer. It costs more than shared hosting for one small site, and it has no email hosting. Check the plan, the visit limit and the refund terms before you pay.
meta.rl_r_buy:
You host client sites as a freelancer or small agency.
You want to hand billing to a client.
You want managed WordPress with a simple dashboard.
meta.rl_r_skip:
You run one small blog and want the lowest price.
You need email hosting in the same plan.
You want a published uptime guarantee.
meta.rl_r_pros:
Billing transfer, Blueprints, staging and cloning for client work.
Nightly backups kept 30 days, with one-click restore.
Free migrations and 24/7 chat support.
A 60-day money-back guarantee listed on the home page.
No renewal jump reported by a third-party review.
meta.rl_r_cons:
Costs more than shared hosting for one small site.
No email hosting and no domain names.
Overage fees of $1 per 1,000 extra visits.
No published uptime guarantee.
WordPress only.
